summary: Built about 1920 on Pico Peak, moved to Killington in the early 1960s, fire use ended in 1984; the standing tower now sits among radio masts on the summit.

access.note: The summit is reached on public trails and the Appalachian Trail, but the tower carries radio equipment and no source says visitors may enter or climb it.

visit.trail_note: Appalachian Trail side trail: 0.4 mile detour with a 240 foot climb. Other routes start from the ski resort.

facts.agency: Vermont Department of Forests and Parks (per the 1963-64 biennial report)

events.note: First constructed on Pico Peak, about 1920 (2012 Vermont report); Trailspotting says the 1920s
Dismantled at Pico and re-erected on Killington; WillhiteWeb gives 1963, the Forest Lookouts entry covers 1963 to 1964
A man went to the Killington fire tower for the summer (newspaper item quoted by the Forest Lookouts page)
A summer dispatcher was to be in charge of the fire tower (newspaper item quoted by the Forest Lookouts page)
A visitor died of an apparent heart attack while climbing the tower (Rutland Daily Herald, June 1973, as quoted by the Forest Lookouts page)
Fire-lookout use discontinued in the fall; one of the final two towers then in use. The tower now carries communications equipment.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2012 report puts the first tower on Pico Peak at about 1920; Trailspotting says the 1920s. Both agree it started on Pico before the move to Killington.
WillhiteWeb gives 1963 for the move, while the Forest Lookouts entry covers 1963 to 1964. The sources do not settle the exact year.

The record conflict pits a gone entry against standing listings. The Forest Lookouts page describes a move to Killington and discontinuation in 1984, not removal. The 2012 report, the 2025 guide and WillhiteWeb all describe a standing tower.

notes_for_editor: Sources are secondary (a state-report transcription on the Forest Lookouts page, a 2012 association report, a blog and a trail guide). No NHLR or FFLOS register entry was found for this tower. Our Eastern US Lookouts record reads gone (dismantled), but the page text we read describes a move, not removal, and the other sources say standing. Worth a human check of the status before publishing. Height and design are unknown; a Facebook post claiming a 35 ft Aermotor was not used. The tower's current owner and climbing rules were not found. The 1963 vs 1963-64 move date is unresolved.
